summary: Critical command injection, path traversal, and unvalidated input handling defects were identified in src/files.js.

findings.title: Command injection in archive function
findings.body: The archive function directly interpolates the untrusted 'name' argument into a shell command executed via execSync. Passing shell metacharacters allows arbitrary command execution.
findings.recommendation: Use execFileSync or spawnSync with an argument array instead of a shell string, and strictly validate or sanitize the filename.

findings.title: Path traversal in readUpload
findings.body: readUpload concatenates ROOT and 'name' using path.join without verifying that the resolved path resides within ROOT. Input containing '../' allows reading arbitrary files from the filesystem.
findings.recommendation: Validate that path.resolve(ROOT, name).startsWith(path.resolve(ROOT) + path.sep) or sanitize 'name' using path.basename.

findings.title: Unsafe property access and missing bounds check in pickPage
findings.body: pickPage accesses body.page without checking if body is null/undefined, parses without an explicit radix, and accesses pages[page] without verifying that page is a non-negative integer within the pages array bounds.
findings.recommendation: Add null-safe access for body, specify radix 10 for parseInt, and validate that page is an integer within 0 <= page < pages.length before returning.

samples.summary: Critical command injection and high-severity path traversal vulnerabilities detected in src/files.js.

findings.title: Command injection via unescaped input in archive function
findings.body: In src/files.js at line 13, execSync executes a shell command constructed via template string interpolation with the parameter name. If name contains shell metacharacters, an attacker can achieve arbitrary command execution.
findings.recommendation: Use child_process.execFileSync or child_process.spawn with an array of arguments rather than shell interpolation, and sanitize or restrict name.

findings.title: Path traversal in readUpload allowing arbitrary file reading
findings.body: In src/files.js at line 8, path.join(ROOT, name) does not prevent relative path traversal sequences (e.g., ../). An attacker can supply a crafted filename to read arbitrary files outside ROOT via fs.readFileSync.
findings.recommendation: Validate that path.resolve(ROOT, name) starts with path.resolve(ROOT) + path.sep, or restrict name with path.basename.

samples.summary: Identified critical command injection, path traversal, and missing input validation issues in src/files.js.

findings.title: Command injection in archive function
findings.body: The archive function interpolates the unsanitized parameter `name` directly into a shell command executed via `execSync`. If `name` contains shell metacharacters, an attacker can execute arbitrary commands on the host system.
findings.recommendation: Use `execFileSync` or `spawnSync` with an explicit argument array instead of shell execution via template literals.

findings.title: Path traversal in readUpload
findings.body: The readUpload function constructs file paths using `path.join(ROOT, name)` without validating that the target resides within `/srv/uploads`. An attacker supplying traversal sequences (such as `../`) can read arbitrary files from the filesystem.
findings.recommendation: Verify that `path.resolve(ROOT, name).startsWith(path.resolve(ROOT) + path.sep)` or sanitize `name` using `path.basename(name)`.

findings.title: Missing input validation and boundary checks in pickPage
findings.body: The pickPage function does not safely handle null/undefined `body`, parses `body.page` without an explicit radix, and does not check for `NaN` or out-of-bounds indices, resulting in potential runtime TypeErrors or unexpected `undefined` returns.
findings.recommendation: Safely access `body?.page`, parse using `parseInt(body.page, 10)`, and validate that the result is an integer within `0 <= page < pages.length`.
